reason: Frozen decision rule requires ALL six conditions for SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. Condition (2) fails: 0/5 TodoMVC variants have ≥2 unique titles (all constant document.title, entropy 0.0 bits). The title falsifier clause (prereg falsifier condition 2) triggers. However, condition (1) passes decisively: 5/5 variants achieve leakage <40% (valid-only 0.213–0.285) with achievable NL 357–394 at 500 raw — the SPA approach is justified for URL-level non-leakage PMI collection. Per-type stratification (link_click 1.00 vs non-link 0.00 on all 628 valid SPA transitions) confirms leakage is entirely action-mix dependent; the 21–28% headline rate reflects the frozen protocol's 27% link share. Fragment-stripping normalization makes link_click leakage tautological on hash-SPAs (all filter links normalize to same base path). All controls pass (Wikipedia 1.00 >80%, vanilla JS 0.2846 <60%, ≥100 raw, ≥5 sessions). Data quality exceeds frozen minimums (168 raw per SPA, 7 sessions). Zero EPIPE crashes across 40 sessions. Audit PASS confirms measurement validity but producer_claim_supported=false: the title-aware PMI ceiling is not justified. The dominant synthetic-to-real gap is partially addressed (SPAs confirmed viable for NL collection) but title-aware PMI remains blocked on TodoMVC. The next experiment should either (a) test URL-only PMI at NL scale on these validated testbeds to directly probe C-WEB-DYNAMICS, or (b) survey production SPAs for title variation to find better testbeds.
